clue.text: Old boring laughter track is ancient

indicators.note: something boring drills its way into another thing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ha is the sound of a laugh
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A grumble that a sitcom's dated canned laughter sounds as if it was recorded centuries ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' sets the abbreviation for old inside the laugh and the railway; 'Old' looks like the definition but 'ancient' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something grey with age and very old is ancient.

clue.text: Animal activist's outburst with a hen mistreated

indicators.note: letters that are mistreated are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal-rights campaigner erupts in anger because a hen has been badly treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistreated' shuffles OUTBURST + A + HEN; the 's is 'is' linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a person who disrupts fox hunting is a campaigner for animals.

clue.text: Imagined axe slashed a rug — it cut into screen

parts.note: to screen a programme is to air it

indicators.note: the word it cuts into the shuffled letters, sitting inside them
a slashed rug is cut up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a rug with an axe, and the slashing reaches a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slashed' makes GUAR from A RUG, and 'cut into' opens it for the pronoun. 'Axe' is slang for a guitar; to screen is to broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: miming guitar playing with no instrument means strumming an axe that exists only in the imagination.

clue.text: Linesman scoffs, holding up end of play

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece holds the other up by sitting above it
the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: A football linesman munches away while stopping play near the end of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesman' is a man of lines, a poet, not a football official.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: a writer of verse lines, here the Irish poet W. B. Yeats.

clue.text: Genius CGI animations, only half animated

indicators.note: animated letters are set moving, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is used

explanation.surface: A film review: the computer animation is clever but only half brought to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps ANIMA of animations; 'animated' shuffles CGI + ANIMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a wizard or brilliant performer is someone of genius in a field.

clue.text: Italian dish gets cold, with Roman and local ingredients

parts.note: macaroni is an Italian pasta dish
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A recipe: an Italian dish served cold with Roman and local ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'ingredients' are languages: macaronic verse mixes Latin with the vernacular.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary term: verse blending Latin words with the local tongue is described this way.

clue.text: Left turn outside of Nashville

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Driving directions: turn left on the edge of Nashville.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who has departed is no longer here.

clue.text: Place for trying zip in novel female attire

parts.note: cases are tried in a court

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard
zip means nothing, O

explanation.surface: A fitting room for trying on clothes, with a zip in some new women's outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside SHE. 'Trying' is a legal trial, not trying on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a plain low-cut women's pump is an item of clothing worn by women.

clue.text: With "p*** off", clergyman gives offence

indicators.note: taking a letter off means removing it from the word

parts.note: a parson is a parish clergyman
the starred word stands for its initial letter

explanation.surface: A vicar swears at someone and causes offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes P from PARSON; the starred expletive is just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Standard article by Tory, with mission to show England overrun by foreigners

parts.note: a standard is a norm
an is the indefinite article
CON is short for Conservative, a Tory
a quest is a mission

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician on a mission to show England is overrun by foreigners.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical event: the 1066 invasion when William's French-speaking forces took over England.

clue.text: Person tripping over hat's cracked a heavy blow

indicators.note: a blow cracked open admits other letters inside

parts.note: a haymaker is a wild heavy punch
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
lid is slang for a hat; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles over a hat and is hit by a heavy blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' opens the heavy blow just after its first letter. 'Tripping' is going on a trip, not stumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a tourist is a person going on a trip.

clue.text: Linguist has appealing quality, university's guaranteed

parts.note: SA is short for sex appeal
U for university with an S
sure means certain, guaranteed

explanation.surface: A language expert is charming and certain of a university place.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand de Saussure was the Swiss founder of modern structural linguistics.

clue.text: Yes, there's trouble for head returning drunk

indicators.note: one word stands in for the head, the first letter, of another
returning means the word read backwards

parts.note: OK means yes
to cause a stink is to cause trouble

explanation.surface: Someone agrees there is trouble on the way home while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns OK into KO; 'for head' replaces its first letter K with STINK.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: a very intoxicated person is said to be this.

clue.text: Bachelor, one completely crazy for oily fruit

parts.note: a complete nut is someone utterly crazy

explanation.surface: A single man is labelled totally mad about some oily fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the white walnut of North America has an oily kernel.

clue.text: Heard where Apple device is charged in orbit?

indicators.note: heard means the words are said out loud

parts.note: Apple devices are named i-something, so its charging point is jokily an i-socket

explanation.surface: Asking where an iPhone is plugged in to charge while in orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orbit' is the bony cavity holding the eye, not a path in space.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy: the orbit is the bony hollow in the skull that holds the eyeball.

clue.text: Technique when shooting is utter flipping blunder

indicators.note: a flipped word is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: to utter a sound is to emit it
a lapse is a slip or error

explanation.surface: A photographer's technique is called a total blooming blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild swear word but turns EMIT into TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Film-making term: shooting frames at long intervals so slow change looks fast.

clue.text: I must be on time for alluring lady

indicators.note: in an across answer, going on another piece means following it

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

explanation.surface: A man insists on being punctual for a date with a seductive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A houri is a beautiful maiden of Islamic paradise, hence a voluptuous woman.

clue.text: Downtrodden, like Labour during Thatcherism

definitions.meaning: Michael Foot led the Labour Party 1980-83, in the early Thatcher years, so Labour was led by him

explanation.surface: A political jibe that Labour was crushed during the Thatcher era.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: trampled on means being beneath people's feet.

clue.text: King wearing drag is a fruitcake!

indicators.note: the clothing wraps round the wearer, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to tote is to carry or haul, drag
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A king in drag is called a nutcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruitcake' looks like slang for a crazy person but is a rich cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a rich layered Continental cake, often with fruit.

clue.text: Rubbish men paid by firm for collections

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: rubbish letters are junk to be sorted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Refuse collectors are paid by a company for collections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' shuffles MEN PAID; 'collections' looks like bin rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of compendium: a compilation or collected digest of material.

clue.text: Still pursuing winning result

indicators.note: pursuing means chasing, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: up means ahead, winning
a still is a photographic shot

explanation.surface: Still chasing a victorious outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the final outcome or consequence of events.

clue.text: Pan to fill has litres in

indicators.note: one piece goes in another

parts.note: to sate is to fill up

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: a pan to be filled with several litres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' is a verb, to criticise harshly, not a cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to slate a show is to savage it in a review.

clue.text: Pick fruit that's bagged etcetera, periodically

indicators.note: bagged means put in a bag, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: Choose fruit to put in a bag, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes every other letter of etcetera, and 'bagged' puts them inside the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a guitar pick is a small plate for plucking strings.

clue.text: Where crooks are beginning to organise a big fiddle

parts.note: criminals are locked in a prison cell

indicators.note: the beginning of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Prisoners start planning a large scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' is a violin, not a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the bass member of the violin family is a large bowed instrument.

clue.text: Trouble afoot, with commander oppressing sailors

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece weighs down on the other from above

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Trouble is brewing as a commander bullies the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' is literal: trouble on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hard painful patch of skin on a toe is a foot problem.

clue.text: Drippy American ex-president cut back security item

parts.note: Andrew Jackson was a US president

indicators.note: back means read in reverse

parts.note: to lop is to cut
a lock keeps things secure

explanation.surface: A wet American former president cuts back on security.
explanation.definitionFit: The US abstract expressionist famous for drip paintings.

clue.text: One lacking in awareness gets punishment

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: sentience is the capacity to perceive, awareness
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A person with no awareness gets penalised.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a penalty handed down by a court.

clue.text: Monarch put on excessive fur

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece put on another follows it

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen dons an over-the-top fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the pelt of a river mammal used as fur.
